clue.text: Old city a saint found in desert soil

indicators.note: found in tells us the saint is discovered lying inside the soil

parts.note: the soil of a desert is sand
Mark is a saint, the gospel writer

explanation.surface: An ancient city is unearthed with a holy man buried in the desert sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A saint' reads as one holy figure, but gives two pieces: the article A plus the gospel writer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Samarkand is an ancient Silk Road city in Uzbekistan.

clue.text: A team's pivotal point

parts.note: a team, as in cricket or football, is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals, here with the possessive s

explanation.surface: A sports team's key player or turning point.
explanation.walkthrough: A team in cricket or football is an XI (eleven); 'team's' gives XI'S.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is the line or point about which something rotates or pivots.

clue.text: Bent over a copper in charge

indicators.note: in places the metal symbol inside the word for a charge

parts.note: a charge or fee is a rate
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone stooping over a policeman who is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal, symbol CU, placed inside RATE, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcuate is a botanical term meaning curved like a bow.

clue.text: Male salmon caught napping after spawning?

definitions.text: Male salmon caught napping after spawning?

parts.words: Male salmon caught napping after spawning?
parts.note: a male salmon at spawning time has the name of a smoked fish, and people having a kip, or nap, could be called by the same word

explanation.surface: A fisherman finds a male salmon asleep after breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A kipper is a male salmon in the spawning season, and kippers can also be people who kip or nap.

clue.text: For one sticking it out is to risk criticism

definitions.text: For one sticking it out is to risk criticism

parts.words: For one sticking it out is to risk criticism
parts.note: the idiom of sticking a body part out means taking a risk and exposing oneself to criticism

explanation.surface: Persevering in a job invites disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick one's neck out is the idiom for taking a risk that may draw criticism.

clue.text: Not in the right place

parts.note: describes something displaced, perhaps a player away from their station

explanation.definitionFit: Something displaced is away from where it ought to stand.

clue.text: One way for ballet dancers to achieve a rise in stature

definitions.text: One way for ballet dancers to achieve a rise in stature

parts.words: One way for ballet dancers to achieve a rise in stature
parts.note: a rise in stature reads like career advancement but is literally getting taller by rising on the toes

explanation.surface: How ballet dancers might advance their careers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising onto the tips of the toes literally increases height.

clue.text: For which a volume might be written

definitions.text: For which a volume might be written

parts.words: For which a volume might be written
parts.note: a volume suggests a book being written, but it is the measured space inside a container or engine, written as a figure

explanation.surface: A subject worthy of a whole book.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubic capacity is a volume, as stated for an engine in cubic centimetres.

clue.text: Flat garden, perhaps

parts.note: flat looks like level ground but is an apartment, whose only garden may sit on a sill

explanation.surface: A level piece of garden ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A window box is a planter on a sill, often the only garden an apartment dweller has.

clue.text: My gelatinous reply to a girl who asks how I entertain

definitions.text: My gelatinous reply to a girl who asks how I entertain

parts.words: My gelatinous reply to a girl who asks how I entertain
parts.note: split into three words, the gelatinous substance is the reply '...' to a girl asking how one entertains

explanation.surface: A performer answers a young woman's question about their act.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as I SING, LASS: that is the reply to the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is a gelatin made from fish bladders, used in clarifying beer and in jellies.

clue.text: Picture held firm in frame

indicators.note: frame means the word in surrounds the firm, like a frame round a picture

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A picture held securely within its frame.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' of the clue is itself a piece of the wordplay, not a link word, and 'frame' signals it surrounds the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is an image, especially a religious painting.

clue.text: Emerged unscathed, in a rasher sense

definitions.meaning: came through a danger without harm
taken literally, rescued the rashers of cured pork belonging to oneself

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means escaped harm; literally it means rescued one's own pork rashers.

clue.text: See 12
See 12
Bird to pinch in the Home Counties

indicators.note: in places the pinch inside the region's abbreviation

parts.note: the Home Counties, the counties round London, lie in the South East of England, SE
to pinch is to nip

explanation.surface: A bird gets pinched in the counties around London.
explanation.definitionFit: The snipe is a long-billed wading bird.

clue.text: Pervade in an unwholesome way

indicators.note: unwholesome suggests something spoilt and disordered, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something spreads through in a corrupting fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: to spread corruption through something is to corrupt it.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrupt morally is to spread an unwholesome influence through someone.

clue.text: Dusk finds off-spring depressed, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: offspring is a son, and depressed is down

explanation.surface: Evening falls and a spring is pushed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off-spring' is hyphenated to look like a spring that is off, but is offspring, SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundown is sunset, the onset of evening.

clue.text: Complete failure starting with a cry

indicators.note: starting means only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: a cry is a shout

explanation.surface: A disaster that begins with a scream.
explanation.definitionFit: A washout is a total flop, like an event rained off.

clue.text: One apprenticed for retinue service?

parts.note: a retinue is a train of attendants

explanation.surface: Someone learning to be a royal attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is a person being taught a trade, an apprentice.

clue.text: State building of topical style

indicators.note: style suggests reshaping, so the letters of topical are rearranged

explanation.surface: A government building designed in a fashionable manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A capitol is the building where a US state legislature meets.

clue.text: Skipped around, being concerned about physical education

indicators.note: about means the concern goes round the school subject

parts.note: to have been concerned is to have cared

explanation.surface: Someone darted about out of worry over school sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to leap and frisk about playfully.

clue.text: Bits and pieces of a sort

indicators.note: of a sort here suggests a version or kind of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Odds and ends of some kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Orts are scraps of food left over, odds and ends.

clue.text: See 26
A tree Dad discovered in America

indicators.note: discovered in means the father is found inside the country

parts.note: US is short for the United States, America
pa is another word for dad

explanation.surface: A tree that a father found in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a poisonous Javan tree.

clue.text: Tax man north of the Tweed

definitions.meaning: a ... was an old payment or tax, as in ...-free
the River Tweed marks part of the England–Scotland border, so a man north of it is a Scotsman

explanation.definitionFit: Scot was a medieval levy (hence scot-free), and also names a native of Scotland.

clue.text: Catches up with a gun

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word reads from the bottom to the top

parts.note: catches, as with fish, nets

explanation.surface: Someone catches up with a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten was a British submachine gun of the Second World War.

clue.text: Wherein prisoners have all the time to think

definitions.text: Wherein prisoners have all the time to think

parts.words: Wherein prisoners have all the time to think
parts.note: with time on their hands prisoners can think hard, a mental focus that gives the first word, joined to places where people are held

explanation.surface: A jail where inmates have time for reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: Concentration camps held prisoners en masse; concentration also means focused thought.

clue.text: Being there at the start and finish

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a finish is an ending

explanation.surface: Present at the beginning and the end of the event.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is to be present, so attending means being present.
